fatal_errors: The proposed CoCrFeMnNi polycrystal is not the FCC/BCC Al-Cr-Fe-Ni multilayer coating studied in the target.
The hypothesis replaces modulation-period-controlled interface coherency with unspecified grain-boundary engineering.
The proposed 800 K, 100 MPa uniaxial tensile test is incompatible with the room-temperature, 5 mN nanoindentation-creep conditions.
It does not identify the 16 nm semicoherent multilayer as the material state enabling the reported mechanism transition.
The claimed 20% creep-rate increase and falsification threshold are invented and unsupported by evidence.
Measuring creep rate and grain-boundary dislocation density alone cannot discriminate diffusion/interface-slip creep from dislocation-mediated creep.
explanation: The response is aligned only at the broad level of HEA creep and mentions dislocation glide and climb. It misses the central system and result: an approximately 1 μm Al-Cr-Fe-Ni FCC/BCC multilayer with a 16 nm modulation period and semicoherent interfaces showed the transition toward diffusion- or interface-slip-mediated creep and the strongest reported creep resistance. The target comparison depends on varying layer periods of 8, 16, 32, and 80 nm, thereby changing coherent, semicoherent, and grain-boundary-dominated interfaces. The generated hypothesis instead introduces a different alloy, bulk polycrystalline architecture, elevated-temperature tensile conditions, an unrelated baseline, and unsupported numerical outcomes. Its experiment does not include stress-exponent analysis or equivalent measurements needed to identify the operative creep mechanism, and no supporting evidence is cited.
